shortDescription: Kinross Gold NYSE:KGC plummets 10.9% in Thursday's trading after cutting production guidance for FY 2026 and 2027, now expecting attributable production of 1.84M-1.86M gold equivalent oz/year, down from its previous forecast of 1.9M-2.1M gold equivalent oz; for Q3, it sees attributable production o…

children: for FY 2026 and 2027, now expecting attributable production of 1.84M-1.86M gold equivalent oz/year, down from its previous forecast of 1.9M-2.1M gold equivalent oz; for Q3, it sees attributable production of ~425K gold equivalent oz.
also said it projects FY 2026 all-in sustaining costs of $1,850-$1,900/oz sold, up from $1,730/oz previously.

The miner said the change to 2026 guidance is concentrated at two smaller assets, La Coipa in Chile and Round Mountain in Nevada, caused by extreme weather and operational challenges, while the balance of the portfolio continues to perform well, led by Paracatu and Tasiast.

partially offset the weaker outlook by increasing its target for returning capital to shareholders from 40% to 50% of free cash flow for 2026; the company said it has returned ~$800M to shareholders YTD, including $655M in share repurchases.
Desjardins analyst Bryce Adams said he views the update "negatively," trimming his price target to C$53 from C$58 while maintaining a Buy rating, noting Kinross'
new production forecast is 8%-9% below consensus and the revised AISC forecast is ~8% above prior guidance.

title: Kinross Gold plunges after cutting 2026-27 production estimates
